question_text: A random sample of people were asked "How many devices have you used to browse the internet in the last month?". The results are displayed in the column graph.

mark_breakdown.desc: Sum all column heights/frequencies from the graph

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The total number of surveyed subjects is the sum of frequencies across all categories.
step_by_step: Read frequencies from the bar graph: 0 devices: 2; 1: 14; 2: 22; 3: 12; 4: 3; 5: 3; 6: 1.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Misreading the bar heights from the vertical axis.

subparts.stem: Find the mode of the data.
subparts.solution: The mode of the data is 2 devices.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The mode is the value with the highest frequency.
step_by_step: Look for the tallest bar on the chart.
The tallest bar corresponds to 2 devices with a frequency of 22.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Giving the frequency (22) instead of the data value (2).

subparts.stem: What percentage of people browsed the internet using 1 or 2 devices?

mark_breakdown.desc: Sum frequencies for 1 and 2 devices and divide by total 57

subparts.solution: $\frac{14 + 22}{57} \times 100\% \approx 63.2\%$ of people browsed the internet using 1 or 2 devices.

step_by_step: Add frequencies for 1 device and 2 devices: $14 + 22 = 36$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including 0 devices or forgetting to divide by 57.

subparts.stem: Describe the distribution of the data.

mark_breakdown.desc: State positive skewness and absence of outliers

subparts.solution: The data is positively skewed with no outliers.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A distribution is positively skewed (skewed right) if the tail on the right side of the peak is longer or fatter than the left side.
step_by_step: Observe the shape: peak is at 2, with a longer tail trailing to the right (up to 6).
Note there are no isolated points far from the rest of the distribution.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing positive skew (tail on the right) with negative skew (tail on the left).
